answer: Pay mint weight only to identities whose local clustering coefficient stays under a bound and that hold at least k edges into clusters they do not control. A farm settling only with its own clones forms a triangle-dense island with no edge leaving it, failing both tests. Missing edges are costly: they must be bought from independent agents at market price, each recording its funder. No atlas of unrelated counterparties appears overnight, and a book spanning umber pigment, cedar timber and milled grain cannot be faked cheaply, since every outside trade leaks the capital trail behind it.
